shipped_rows.title_o: Women Are More Likely to Wear Red or Pink at Peak Fertility

blind_target.authors: Tracy, J. L., & Beall, A. T.
blind_target.title: The impact of weather on women’s tendency to wear red or pink when at high risk for conception
blind_target.evidence_quote: Having found inconclusive evidence in Study 1 for an effect of conception risk on the likelihood of wearing red or pink on relatively cold days, in Study 2 (Analysis I) we used data from a large sample collected online between February 2015 and May 2015 to more closely replicate Beall and Tracy (2013) and Tracy and Beall (2014).
blind_target.outcome_quote: The studies we presented here, which incorporated conceptual replications, close replications, and extended replications of the original studies reporting that women are more likely to wear red or pink at peak fertility (Beall & Tracy, 2013; Tracy & Beall, 2014), failed to reliably confirm the conjecture that women advertise their ovulatory status by wearing red, even on relatively cold days.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors give an overall failed-to-confirm verdict explicitly covering both original papers and all conceptual, close, and extended attempts. This overall verdict governs despite isolated supportive comparisons.

luna_triage.reason: The source explicitly conducts close and extended retests of Tracy and Beall (2014), whose weather-moderated red/pink clothing finding is distinct from the supplied Beall and Tracy (2013) original. The sole shipped row represents the earlier 2013 paper, not the 2014 paper directly retested; the 2014 work is independently identified in the source references.
luna_triage.omission_quote: A successive failure to replicate this finding led them to explore the possibility that ovulating women are more likely than non-ovulating women to wear red on cold days, though not on warm days (Tracy & Beall, 2014).
luna_triage.identity_quote: TracyJL, & BeallAT (2014). The impact of weather on women’s tendency to wear red or pink when at high risk for conception. PLoS ONE, 9(2), e88852.
luna_triage.duplicate_quote: BeallAT, & TracyJL (2013). Women are more likely to wear red or pink at peak fertility.
